name: Feed
description: A scrollable section that automatically loads new content as the user scrolls, presenting content as a series of article elements.

keyboard_interactions.action: Move focus to the next article
Move focus to the previous article
Move focus to first focusable element after the feed
Move focus to first focusable element before the feed

roles.description: Identifies the container as a feed
Identifies each piece of content as an article

required_attributes.description: Provides accessible name for the feed
References elements providing a distinguishing label

optional_attributes.description: References the primary content elements of the article
Article's position number within the feed
Total number of loaded articles, or -1 if undetermined
true during loading; false when complete

notes: Prefer a plain list of articles with an explicit 'Load more' button. It is simpler, keyboard-friendly, and does not trap anyone below the fold.
THE infinite-scroll problem (RAWeb 12.9): if content loads forever, the footer is unreachable by keyboard and by screen reader. A 'Load more' button fixes this; auto-loading on scroll does not.
aria-busy='true' on the feed while inserting items, back to 'false' when done — otherwise assistive technologies read a half-built DOM.
Each article needs role='article', a heading, aria-labelledby pointing at that heading, and aria-posinset/aria-setsize. Use aria-setsize='-1' when the total is unknown.
Announce loading in a separate polite live region (RAWeb 7.5), never with aria-live on the feed itself — that would announce every inserted article.
Do not move focus when new items load. The user is reading.
native_element: none — a plain <ul> of <article>s with a 'Load more' button is usually better

raweb_criteria.reason: feed/article roles and aria-busy must be exposed.
Loading and 'N new items' are status messages and must be announced without moving focus.
Each article needs a heading — the feed is navigated by heading, and aria-labelledby should point at it.
Page Down/Up move between articles; the feed must be fully keyboard operable.
An infinite feed can trap keyboard users: content below (the footer) may never be reachable if new items load forever.
A feed that auto-updates with new content is moving content — the user must be able to stop it.
